messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide on how to **generate** (but not necessarily execute) a RESTful API request for the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. The instructions assume you have already logged into the Nexus Dashboard UI and have the necessary permissions to view the API Explorer. --- ## 1. Locate the API Explorer | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | In the left‑hand navigation pane, click **“Developer”** → **“API Explorer”**. | | 2 | If you don’t see “API Explorer”, it may be hidden under the **“More”** dropdown; expand it and enable the feature. | > **Tip:** The API Explorer is a built‑in tool that lets you browse all available endpoints, view their documentation, and generate sample requests. --- ## 2. Find the Desired Endpoint | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | In the API Explorer search bar, type **“device connector versions”** or the exact API name **“get information of device connector versions”**. | | 2 | Click the matching result. You should now see the endpoint details. | ### Typical Endpoint Path ``` GET /api/v1/device-connector/versions ``` > The actual path may vary slightly depending on your deployment. The API Explorer will display the exact URL pattern. --- ## 3. Inspect the Endpoint Details | Section | What to Look For | |---------|------------------| | **HTTP Method** | `GET` | | **Path** | `/api/v1/device-connector/versions` | | **Query Parameters** | None (or optional filters such as `?status=active`) | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer `
`Accept: application/json` | | **Response Schema** | JSON object containing an array of connector version objects. | > The API Explorer shows a live preview of the response schema, so you can copy the JSON structure if needed. --- ## 4. Generate the Sample Request | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | Click the **“Generate Request”** button (usually located at the top right of the endpoint pane). | | 2 | A modal pops up showing the full request in multiple formats: | | | • **cURL**
• **Python (requests)**
• **JavaScript (fetch)**
• **Postman** collection snippet | | 3 | Copy the snippet that matches your preferred language or tool. | ### Example cURL Snippet ```bash curl -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions" \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " ``` ### Example Python (requests) Snippet ```python import requests url = "https:///api/v1/device-connector/versions" headers = { "Accept": "application/json", "Authorization": "Bearer " } response = requests.get(url, headers=headers) print(response.json()) ``` > Replace `` with your actual host (e.g., `dashboard.cisco.com`) and `` with a valid OAuth token. --- ## 5. (Optional) Export the Request to Postman If you prefer to test the endpoint in Postman: 1. In the generated request modal, click **“Export to Postman”**. 2. Postman will automatically create a new request in your workspace with the correct method, URL, headers, and body. --- ## 6. Authentication & Authorization | Item | How to Obtain | |------|---------------| | **Access Token** | Use the **OAuth 2.0** flow in the Nexus Dashboard UI or via the **“Get Token”** endpoint. | | **Client ID / Secret** | Provided when you register an application in the **“Developer”** section. | | **Scope** | Ensure the scope includes `read:device_connector_versions`. | > **Important:** The token must be refreshed before it expires (typically 60 minutes). Use the **“Refresh Token”** endpoint if needed. --- ## 7. Verify the Response Once you send the request (via cURL, Python, Postman, etc.), you should receive a JSON payload similar to: ```json { "data": [ { "id": "dcv-001", "name": "Connector v1.0", "status": "active", "releaseDate": "2024-01-15", "description": "Initial release." }, { "id": "dcv-002", "name": "Connector v1.1", "status": "deprecated", "releaseDate": "2024-03-22", "description": "Deprecated in favor of v2.0." } ], "meta": { "totalCount": 2, "page": 1, "pageSize": 50 } } ``` > The exact fields may differ; refer to the API Explorer’s response schema for the definitive structure. --- ## 8. Troubleshooting Common Issues | Symptom | Likely Cause | Fix | |---------|--------------|-----| | **401 Unauthorized** | Token missing or expired | Refresh token or re‑authenticate | | **404 Not Found** | Wrong endpoint path | Double‑check the URL in the API Explorer | | **400 Bad Request** | Incorrect headers or query params | Ensure `Accept: application/json` and any required params are present | | **500 Internal Server Error** | Backend issue | Contact Cisco support or check system logs | --- ## 9. Automating the Request (Optional) If you want to embed this request in a script or CI/CD pipeline, you can use the **Python snippet** above and schedule it with cron or a workflow runner. Make sure to store the access token securely (e.g., environment variable, secrets manager). --- ### Quick Summary 1. **Open API Explorer** → Search for “device connector versions”. 2. **View endpoint** → Note method (`GET`), path, headers. 3. **Generate Request** → Copy cURL/Python snippet. 4. **Authenticate** → Add `Authorization: Bearer `. 5. **Send & Verify** → Expect JSON response with connector version data. That’s it! You now know how to generate a RESTful API request for the *Get information of device connector versions* endpoint in Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy querying!
